title: Going away to high school in Topeka and falling for math
summary: He persuades his mother to send him to a school in Topeka, where good teachers make algebra and geometry click and he takes four years of math.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So when I went... I don't remember too much of the math I had in the seventh and eighth grades in Muskogee. So I talked my mother into letting me go off to school. A buddy of mine had gone to Wilberforce, came back and told me how good it was going off to school. So I found out about this school in Topeka, so I talked my mother into sending me there. My father wanted me to wait a year later. But my mother said, "Don't worry about it. You go on."

So I did. I went and made that... I started almost like you do it in college. I started in my freshman year. And how I got ahold of all them good teachers, I'll never know. I had one woman teacher, one female teacher, and one guy named McCord. He had a knot on his head. And we always thought all that knowledge was up there in that knot. And they were... To me they were so great, because the one thing they told us in the freshman class, he said, "Algebra is only arithmetic in algebraic form." Well, I had my arithmetic, so I flew through that algebra. Then I got to geometry... I think that's when we had the lady teacher. And she told us that geometry was just another phase of
arithmetic where you deal with the angles and lines and circles.
I got so crazy about math after my first two years in high school, I took four years of math in high school. And after I finished high school, I had one year of college to my credit.
